title: Null Handling and Three-Valued Logic
description: CQL's null is UNKNOWN, not false. Learn how null flows through comparisons, Boolean operators, and functions — and how Coalesce, is null, and Count each treat it. This is the single most common source of silent eCQM bugs.
learningObjectives: Test for null with 'is null' on absent fields
See how null != x collapses to null (not false)
Apply the and/or truth tables with null operands
Observe Count skipping null list elements

hints.message: Patient.deceased is null — this patient has no deathDate, so the field is absent (null).
null != 'x' is null (UNKNOWN) — not false! But watch the results panel: the row is still present.
Three-valued and: null and false = false (false wins), null and true = null.
Three-valued or: null or true = true (true wins), null or false = null.
not null is still null — negation does not make unknown known.
Coalesce(a, b, c, ...) returns the first non-null argument, or null if all are null.
Absent JSON fields are null in CQL — Patient.telecom is null for this patient.
Coalesce(Patient.deceased.value, 'still alive') — .value on a null field stays null, so the default wins.
Count({null, 'a', null, 'b'}) = 2 — Count skips null elements.
(X is null) is true — wrap an is-null test in is true to get a definite Boolean you can branch on.
